## Partner v0.3.4

This release makes the web search engine set configurable: alongside the built-in presets you can now add your own JSON-based search engines with a URL template and result-field mapping, or alias a preset under your own name. The prompt and web settings editors moved into dialogs, and the documentation across all three languages was streamlined.

- **Configurable web search engines:** Settings now store an optional per-engine list. Each entry is either an enabled built-in preset (optionally renamed) or a custom engine defined by an http(s) URL template with a single `{query}` marker, plus a JSON path to the result list and field mappings for title, link and snippet. Entries with neither preset nor template are ignored; validation rejects duplicate or empty ids, malformed templates, and unsafe or local addresses. When a configured list exists it fully replaces the default engine set.
- **Settings and prompts UI:** The main-agent and sub-agent prompt editors, and the web engine list editor, now open in dialogs instead of inline panels, with focus returned to the trigger button on close. Toggling a preset engine edits the row in the configured list; a "restore default engines" action rebuilds the list from the built-in defaults.
- **Documentation:** The READMEs and most doc pages were condensed in all three languages, the services documentation was restructured into a shorter layout, and mangled language-navigation lines in the pet, voice and services pages were repaired. The schedules documentation now states the exact preconditions under which a direct `web_fetch` status can serve as 5xx/2xx anomaly evidence (requests without credentials or a query string).

## Notes

- **Test infrastructure:** The desktop CDP wire tests now assemble fragmented WebSocket frames before parsing, so message handling that arrives in multiple chunks is no longer misread.
- Engine configuration and validation are covered by new API and engine unit tests.
- There is no dedicated web-engine documentation page yet; the [schedules](https://github.com/Jaspersol/partner/blob/v0.3.4/doc/schedules.en.md) and [services](https://github.com/Jaspersol/partner/blob/v0.3.4/doc/services.en.md) pages cover `web_fetch` behavior.
